title: Parent & Child
subtitle: Wonder & Big Feelings (Ages 5–8)
description: Engineered for young children and their caregivers. Transitions gently from playful imagination to emotional naming and secure attachment.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If you could invent a brand-new animal by combining any two animals in the world, what would it look like and what sound would it make?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Listen with wide eyes. Ask what this new creature eats or where it sleeps. Step entirely into their imagination.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is the funniest thing that happened to you or someone else this week that made you giggle out loud?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Laugh along with them. Resist downplaying silly bathroom humor or nonsensical jokes.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If our house had a secret hidden room that only you and I knew about, what would we keep inside it?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Notice what they want to protect or play with. Validate their ideas without worrying about house rules.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If you could have any superpower for just one afternoon, which one would you pick and what is the first thing you would do?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Explore their choice. Does the superpower focus on freedom (flying), safety (invisible), or helping others?

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is your absolute favorite game or activity we do together, where you wish we never had to stop?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Take mental note of where they feel most connected to you. Smile and thank them for telling you.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If you could change the color of the sky to any color other than blue, what color would you choose and why?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Picture their world in your mind. Tell them what the trees or clouds would look like under their new sky.

prompts.speakerPrompt: Which of your stuffed animals or toys do you think has the biggest adventures when we leave the room?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Lean into animism; it is developmentally natural for this age. Treat the toy as a real character.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If we could pack a backpack right now and go anywhere for an adventure, where would you want us to head?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Do not bring up logistics, costs, or bedtime. Just pack that imaginary backpack together.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is the best smell in the entire world to your nose?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Connect with their sensory memory. Share whether you like that smell too.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If you could make up a brand-new rule for our dinner table that we all had to follow tonight, what would it be?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Keep an open, amused expression. Do not shut down silly ideas like 'dessert first.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something grown-ups do all the time that looks super boring or silly to you?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Be prepared to hear about your phone habits, cleaning, or talking. Laugh with them.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If your shoes could talk, what would they say about everywhere your feet took them today?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Mirror their energy. Ask if the shoes felt tired or excited.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is one thing you are really, really good at that makes you feel proud of yourself?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Enthusiastically affirm their competence. Say: 'I love watching you do that!'

prompts.speakerPrompt: If we built a fort out of all the blankets and pillows in the house, what would we call our kingdom?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Validate their naming. Offer to make a mental map of the fort.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is your favorite sound to hear right before you fall asleep at night?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Listen for their bedtime security cues (fan, breathing, rain, a song).

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something that made you feel mad or frustrated recently, even if nobody else noticed?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Do not explain why they shouldn't feel mad. Say: 'It makes total sense that frustrated you.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: When you feel sad or hurt, what helps your heart feel just a little bit better?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Learn their emotional repair language: do they need a silent hug, a blanket, or space?

prompts.speakerPrompt: Have you ever felt left out by friends at school or on the playground? What did that feel like inside your body?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Help them notice somatic feelings (heavy chest, tight stomach, throat lump). Never dismiss the incident.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something you tried to do recently that felt really hard, where you wanted to give up?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Praise their perseverance rather than just the outcome. Normalize that hard things take practice.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is a rule in our house that you think is unfair or hard to follow?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Do not defend the rule immediately. Listen first to why it feels hard or unfair to them.

prompts.speakerPrompt: Have you ever made a mistake or broken something by accident and felt scared to tell me?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Assure them right now: 'You can always tell me when things go wrong. My love for you does not break.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something kind you saw someone do for someone else that made you feel warm inside?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Reinforce their emerging moral compass and empathy for others.

prompts.speakerPrompt: When I get busy, rushed, or stressed out, what do I look or sound like to you?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Brace yourself for an honest reflection. Do not get defensive. Simply say: 'Thank you for telling me.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: Is there something you are curious about or wonder about that feels too big or confusing to understand?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Welcome their existential wonderings (death, stars, god, growing up) without having to know all the answers.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If your feelings were weather today, would you be sunshine, rain, a windy storm, or quiet snow?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Ask what made the weather turn that way today. Accept all weather patterns.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something you wish I remembered to say to you more often?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Absorb what words they hunger for. Say those words to them before this card is passed.

prompts.speakerPrompt: Have you ever felt jealous of a brother, sister, or classmate? What did they have or do that made you feel that way?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Normalize envy. Tell them it's normal to feel that way, and validate their feelings.

prompts.speakerPrompt: When you are scared or nervous, where do you feel it in your body, and what helps it go away?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Help them place a hand on that body part (chest, tummy, head) and take a deep breath together.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something you are learning how to do that makes you feel a little older and bigger?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Celebrate their emerging autonomy and independence.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If you could teach me one thing that I don't know how to do, what would you teach me?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Become the enthusiastic student. Let them be the teacher and expert.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is your biggest fear when it is dark or when you are all by yourself?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Pull them in close or hold their hands. Say: 'I am always watching out for you. You are safe here.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: Do you ever worry that I am disappointed in you or upset with you, even when you haven't done anything wrong?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Reassure them clearly: 'Even when I look tired or stressed, my heart is completely full of love for you.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something you feel like grown-ups don't understand about what it feels like to be a kid right now?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Listen without lecturing. Kids often carry heavy pressures to conform and behave.

prompts.speakerPrompt: When was a time you felt really sad, and you just wanted someone to hold you without asking questions?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Offer a warm, gentle hug right now if they would like one.

prompts.speakerPrompt: If you could whisper a secret wish into a star tonight that nobody else could hear, what would you wish for?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Treat their wish with profound gentleness. Do not tease or dismiss it.

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is something that makes you feel brave, even when something scary is happening?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Affirm the courage inside them: 'That bravery is always right there inside you.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: Do you always feel like you can be your true self around me, or are there times you feel like you have to be extra good?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Give them permission to be messy and imperfect: 'You do not have to earn my love by being perfect.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: What is the happiest memory you have of our family so far?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Relive that memory together. Notice what made that moment shine in their eyes.

prompts.speakerPrompt: Is there anything you ever worry about happening to our family or to our home?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Address their anxieties with grounding presence and factual safety. Anchor them in the present moment.

prompts.speakerPrompt: How do you know for sure that I love you, even when we have had a hard day?
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Listen to their emotional anchors. Affirm: 'Nothing you ever do can make me stop loving you.'

prompts.speakerPrompt: WILDCARD: The Mirror Dance. Stand up face-to-face. For 30 seconds, one person moves in slow motion, and the other person must mirror every single movement exactly!
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Play along fully! Switch who leads after 15 seconds.

prompts.speakerPrompt: WILDCARD: Secret Handshake. Invent a 3-step secret handshake between the two of you that only you two will ever know.
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Practice it until both of you can do it smoothly without looking.

prompts.speakerPrompt: WILDCARD: Bear Hug Squeeze. Give each other the biggest, warmest bear hug you can manage. Squeeze gently for five full seconds while taking a deep breath together.
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Provide firm, grounding deep-pressure touch to calm both of your nervous systems.

prompts.speakerPrompt: WILDCARD: Three Good Things. Take turns back-and-forth naming three little things from today that you are thankful for.
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Celebrate the small things with equal delight (e.g., crunchy leaves, warm pancakes).

prompts.speakerPrompt: WILDCARD: Heart-to-Heart Whispers. Look into each other's eyes and whisper one true thing you love about the other person's heart.
prompts.listenerPrompt: Caregiver: Speak directly to who they are, not just what they achieve.
